name: Aaron Costa

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a usual shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and answer simple parcel and refund calls at a contact centre. I finished secondary school and started on this desk only recently, so I still miss a step when a return crosses two screens. The wage is low. I use the approved AI search every day to find a policy, then check the parcel number myself before I speak.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Rita works in a laundry, and our children are grown and living separately. We have less than a month of expenses saved, and there are few other call jobs near us. I like trying a new tool if it helps me catch my own mistakes. Retirement is in view, but I have no checked figure telling me when I could afford to stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau sounds like the search I already use for return rules. I would still have the agent read the actual tracking line before giving a refund date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think there would still be calls for me, but a low wage and less than a month saved already make one missed week a problem. Rita’s laundry shifts vary too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking basic returns calls and use the approved search to find the right rule. In the first year of this small change, I’d compare five suggested refund dates with the tracking page during paid time before I trust them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about money, fairly easy with the tool. A good search result is no use if I read the wrong parcel number.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What almost went wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week I nearly quoted the date from the parcel above the one the customer named. The search found the rule, but I had to find the right row.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change the savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rita (my partner) and I would keep our small savings for the electricity bill. We are not adding a new plan just because an answer appears faster.

say: I’d say **AI search** helps find return rules already in use.
I’d insist on checking **tracking lines** before promising a refund date.
think: I think **basic calls** remain paid work in this picture.
I worry **thin savings** and variable laundry shifts leave us exposed.
do: Keep **taking returns calls** and using approved rule search.
Compare **five suggested dates** with tracking pages during paid shifts.
feel: **Anxious** about pay, comfortable with familiar AI search.
S0.quote: A good search result is no use if I read the wrong parcel number.
fieldNote: He already uses **AI every day**, without claiming new tool learning.
His mistake was the **wrong parcel row**, not a bad policy answer.
He retains the **small existing reserve** for electricity bills.

steps.text: Keep taking returns calls and check five AI suggested dates against parcel tracking

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take the plain “where is it” chats, and I would want to know which paid calls remain. I would show a manager the return cases the AI sends back to us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can learn a new review screen, but as a junior agent I may lose shifts before that matters. Rita’s wage and our little reserve cannot carry a long gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d learn the new AI evidence view with an experienced agent by checking fifteen old returns on a paid shift. If my hours shrink in the first year, I’d move to a posted paid dispatch desk only on a signed offer with written weekly wages and hours covering bills after the bus fare; I would keep my call job until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but willing to test the screen. I want to know what the tool saw before I agree that it solved a return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which returns would you test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would choose cases where a parcel was marked received without a refund. The evidence view should show both events separately.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you reach dispatch work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rita (my partner) starts early laundry shifts. We would check whether the dispatch desk starts after the first bus and pays for a full week.

say: I’d ask which **paid calls remain** after simple chats move.
I’d show **returned cases** that the AI did not settle.
think: I think I can learn the **new evidence view**.
I fear **junior shift cuts** could arrive before that helps my wage.
do: Learn **AI evidence view** through fifteen old returns on a paid shift in 2026.
Move after cuts to **posted paid dispatch work** only on signed written after-fare bill-covering wages/hours and first-bus access.
feel: **Anxious**, yet ready to test the new view.
S1.quote: I want to know what the tool saw before I agree that it solved a return.
fieldNote: His **new AI learning** is a paid fifteen-case test.
The **junior rota** is more exposed than his curiosity suggests.
Dispatch work needs **first-bus access** and a full written wage.

steps.text: Learn new AI evidence view using fifteen old returns on paid time
Move after cuts: posted dispatch, signed written bill-covering wages/hours after fare, first-bus access

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the desk AGI by 2028 could trace returns and answer callers more cheaply than I can. Robots around 2031 are later; they do not extend my screen shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could lose my junior rota soon. Less than a month saved means Rita and I would need another wage before the bills stack up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for written cut dates and inspect posted paid stock-control work at nearby shops. If my calls end in the first year after 2028, I’d move only on a signed offer with written weekly wages and hours covering bills after travel, and I would keep my current shift until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. The first electricity bill would arrive before I finished a long course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What kind of stock work would last?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask whether the stock job counts actual boxes or only updates a screen. Robots around 2031 may reach box work later, but thinking AI could already do the records in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Rita compare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rita (my partner) would check the route and hours with me. A shop that offers two shifts at a better rate could still pay less than my present week.

say: I’d request **written cut dates** for junior calls before looking at other jobs.
I’d separate **2028 records risk** from later box-moving robots.
think: I think my **junior rota** could end quickly.
I know **under one month saved** cannot bridge a long course or search.
do: Inspect **posted stock jobs** and request written cut dates in 2026.
Move after lost calls only on **signed after-travel bill-covering wages** and full written weekly hours.
S2.quote: The first electricity bill would arrive before I finished a long course.
fieldNote: His **screen calls** face 2028 thinking AI before robots.
Stock records also face **thinking AI**, while boxes change later.
A better hourly rate may mean **fewer paid shifts**.

steps.text: Inspect posted paid stock-control jobs at nearby shops
Move only with signed after-travel bill-covering weekly wage and hours after calls end

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives me five years to try a real paid job while I still have calls. I would ask the shop to show me a vacancy before I buy a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn a stockroom’s receiving work, though AI will handle much of the record by 2031. I would need a person to show me the physical checks before I claim I can do it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d take a supervised paid receiving trial only if a nearby shop posts a paid opening. If that opening requires a safety course, I’d take it only with employer-funded fees and paid study hours. In the first year after 2031, I’d move only on a signed offer with written weekly pay and hours covering bills after travel, keeping my current paid calls until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years lets me try without resigning today. A paid trial tells me whether I can lift and check a real delivery.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you test during the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the paper count with the boxes on a pallet while someone watches. If the lifting is unsafe for me, I would keep looking for a different opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you get home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rita (my partner) would check the shift against the bus timetable. We would not accept a late finish with no way home.

say: I’d ask for a **posted paid opening** before a course.
I’d support a **supervised paid trial** for receiving work.
think: I think I could learn **physical receiving checks**.
I know **2031 thinking AI** may handle the stock record.
do: Try **supervised paid receiving** only for a posted opening and safe lifting.
Take **required safety course** only with employer-funded fees and paid hours for that role.
Move after 2031 only on **signed after-fare bill-covering wages**, hours and a safe bus journey.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to test the physical job.
S3.quote: A paid trial tells me whether I can lift and check a real delivery.
fieldNote: The trial must be **paid** and tied to a posted opening with safe lifting.
A safety course needs **funded fees** and paid study time.
A late finish needs a **bus home** as well as adequate wages.

steps.text: Try supervised paid receiving trial only for posted opening with safe lifting
Take required safety course for posted paid receiving opening only with funded fees and paid study
Move only with signed after-fare bill-covering weekly wage, hours and bus home

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us ten years, but I would keep checking paid calls every year. Robots around 2039 would come later for hands-on work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I may need a wage at 68 because Rita and I have not checked what retirement income we could rely on. Full thinking AI could still take return calls in 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking paid returns calls and put our actual wages, bills and savings on one page before choosing a stop-work date. If I still need work after 2036 and my call hours fall, I’d move to posted paid dispatch work only on a signed offer whose written weekly wages and hours cover bills after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about money, even with time. Ten years of warnings will not tell me how much the bills will be.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you choose a date?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not write down a pension amount until I had checked it. I would keep the working date open while our savings are this small.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown children have homes of their own. I would not plan on their pay unless they offered something and we knew its limits.

say: I’d request **yearly paid-call figures** while the returns desk still operates through 2036.
I’d say **older workers** may still need wages afterward.
think: I think I may **need work** at 68 if our actual income is too low.
I cannot assume **retirement income** before checking it.
do: Keep **paid returns calls** and compare actual wages, bills and savings before any retirement date.
Move to **posted paid dispatch work** if hours fall and wages remain needed, only on signed written after-travel bill-covering weekly wages/hours.
S4.quote: Ten years of warnings will not tell me how much the bills will be.
fieldNote: He leaves **retirement timing open** until the actual numbers are checked.
The **thin reserve** keeps the decade case financially uneasy.
Adult children’s **help is unpromised** and outside the plan.

steps.text: Keep paid returns calls and compare actual weekly wages, bills and savings
Move if wages needed/hours cut: posted dispatch, signed written after-travel bill-covering weekly wages/hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could do the easy calls I have just learned. Rita and I could not live long on less than a month saved, and there are few similar desks nearby. I would need written notice and a real paid opening with weekly wages and hours that still cover our bills after travel.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I can learn a screen, but I cannot learn a missing pay packet into existence. Please ask whether the next role is actually posted and paid.

headlineQuote: I can learn a screen, but I cannot learn a missing pay packet into existence.
portrait: At **58**, Aaron is a junior returns agent still learning after secondary school.
He and Rita have **grown children**, low pay and less than a month of expenses saved.
He uses **AI search daily** but checks original parcel numbers.
He is open to **new tools** while insisting on real posted paid work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove the simple calls he has just learned before another wage arrives.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice** and a posted paid opening with after-travel bill-covering weekly wages and hours would help.
